raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantB: This is Mark.
ParticipantA: Oh, hi Mark. This is Sarah.
ParticipantB: Yeah, sure. What's up?
ParticipantA: Just wanted to chat about family life. You have kids?
ParticipantB: Yep, two boys, ages 7 and 5.
ParticipantA: Nice. I have three girls, oldest is ten now.
ParticipantB: Ten? That's not that long ago. We're only a year apart.
ParticipantA: Yeah, crazy how fast they grow. Sometimes I still remember when I carried them all.
ParticipantB: Exactly. My little one was carried too. It's wild.
ParticipantA: Do you feel like you have it figured out with parenting?
ParticipantB: Honestly? A little skeptical sometimes. My cousin drove a school bus for years, same as me. He says the kids are tougher than we give them credit for. He's still talking about it.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? That's interesting. I feel like I made up my mind way back when I was younger about being an electrician. Just knew I had to do it.
ParticipantB: Oh, electrician? That's cool. I don't know much about the work, but it sounds like you'd be around people a lot, or just alone?
ParticipantA: Mostly alone, mostly just me, my truck, and the job. But I like it. I have so many opinions about wiring and stuff. It just feels right.
ParticipantB: Huh. My cousin says the job is hard because you can't fix everything just by talking to people.
ParticipantA: That's true. Sometimes you just have to get the job done, no matter what. But I love figuring out the problems. It's satisfying.
ParticipantB: Yeah, my cousin says that's the same with kids. You can't just wish them to behave; you gotta set boundaries.
ParticipantA: Yeah, boundaries are key. I think about that a lot with the girls. They test me every day.
ParticipantB: Totally. My older one just asked for a new bike this week. I said no, she cried for twenty minutes, then got over it.
ParticipantA: Haha, that sounds familiar. My youngest did that yesterday. Took me an hour to explain why we couldn't buy her another toy.
ParticipantB: Man, you're tough! I'm starting to think I need some of that "just get it done" energy.
ParticipantA: Maybe. But hey, you're doing the bus thing too, right? That's a people job.
ParticipantB: Yep. Different kind of tough. Gotta keep the schedule, keep the kids happy, deal with parents.
ParticipantA: Sounds intense. Do you think it's better than being alone with a job?
ParticipantB: Maybe? Hard to say. My cousin says he loves the bus life, but he's definitely burned out sometimes.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I guess I burn out too sometimes. Just need a break from the shop.
ParticipantB: True. Well, glad we talked. My cousin would probably tell me to quit if I was listening.
ParticipantA: Haha, yeah. Well, take care, Mark.
ParticipantB: You too, Sarah. Take it easy.
ParticipantA: Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
